sources.entry: The MIPS R10000 Superscalar Microprocessor - Shows rename, the active list and precise branch recovery fitted together in one shipped out-of-order core.

summary.title: The Mips R10000 superscalar microprocessor
summary.one_liner: How the MIPS R10000 combined speculative, out-of-order execution with in-order graduation, precise exceptions, and a nonblocking two-level cache hierarchy.
keywords: how does an out-of-order cpu work
takeaways: The R10000 fetches and decodes four instructions per cycle and issues them dynamically to five pipelined execution units.
Instructions execute speculatively beyond branches but graduate in order, which keeps exceptions precise.
Despite out-of-order execution, the design preserves sequential memory consistency.
Speculative address calculation and early cache refills help hide memory latency in applications with poor locality.
The memory system uses two levels of set-associative, write-back caches with nonblocking behavior.
summary.summary: This IEEE Xplore page is the abstract and metadata for a paper describing the MIPS R10000, a dynamic superscalar microprocessor implementing the 64-bit MIPS 4 ISA. The abstract explains the front end (four instructions fetched and decoded per cycle), the out-of-order issue to five fully pipelined execution units, and speculative execution past branches. It also covers how in-order graduation keeps precise exceptions and sequential memory consistency, and how the nonblocking two-level write-back cache hierarchy hides memory latency. The page text provides no further detail beyond the abstract.
